card.name: Words introducing a following clause
card.fires_on: Small words that open a new clause right after a noun or phrase, such as you, they, unless, if, when, or a comma. They often mark a condition or a relative clause, like 'any size you want' or 'unless the infusion is initiated'.

modes.label: Relative clause subject
modes.description: A pronoun such as you or they starts a clause that modifies the noun just before it.
modes.example: talk to a friend or a teacher that<< you>> can trust about your feelings.

modes.label: Condition words
modes.description: Unless, if, or when begins a condition or exception after a statement.
modes.example: is recommended only<< if>> medical care can be readily accessed.

modes.label: Comma after instructions
modes.description: A comma after a noun leads into a qualifying phrase.
modes.example: But to the married I give instructions<<,>> not I, but the Lord, that
